entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: 1Sa 21:1-7 . David, at Nob, Obtains of Ahimelech Hallowed Bread.

entries.heading: 2. The king hath commanded me a business, and hath said unto me, Let no man know
entries.text: 2. The king hath commanded me a business, and hath said unto me, Let no man know --This was a direct falsehood, extorted through fear. David probably supposed, like many other persons, that a lie is quite excusable which is told for the sole purpose of saving the speaker's life. But what is essentially sinful, can never, from circumstances, change its immoral character; and David had to repent of this vice of lying ( Ps 119:29 ).

entries.heading: 4. there is hallowed bread
entries.text: 4. there is hallowed bread --There would be plenty of bread in his house; but there was no time to wait for it. "The hallowed bread" was the old shew-bread, which had been removed the previous day, and which was reserved for the use of the priests alone ( Le 24:9 ). Before entertaining the idea that this bread could be lawfully given to David and his men, the high priest seems to have consulted the oracle ( 1Sa 22:10 ) as to the course to be followed in this emergency. A dispensation to use the hallowed bread was specially granted by God Himself.

entries.heading: 5. these three days
entries.text: 5. these three days --as required by law ( Ex 19:15 ). David and his attendants seem to have been lurking in some of the adjoining caves, to elude pursuit, and to have been, consequently, reduced to great extremities of hunger. the bread is in a manner common --that is, now that it is no longer standing on the Lord's table. It is eaten by the priests, and may also, in our circumstances, be eaten by us. yea, though it were sanctified this day in the vessel --that is, though the hallowed bread had been but newly placed on the vessel, the ritual ordinance would have to yield to the great law of necessity and mercy (see on Mt 12:3 ; also see Mr 2:25; Lu 6:3 ).

entries.heading: 6. there was no bread there
entries.text: 6. there was no bread there --in the tabernacle. The removal of the old and the substitution of the new bread was done on the Sabbath ( Le 24:8 ), the loaves being kept warm in an oven heated the previous day.

entries.heading: 7. Doeg, an Edomite
entries.text: 7. Doeg, an Edomite --who had embraced the Hebrew religion. detained before the Lord --at the tabernacle, perhaps, in the performance of a vow, or from its being the Sabbath, which rendered it unlawful for him to prosecute his journey. the chiefest of the herdmen that belonged to Saul --Eastern monarchs anciently had large possessions in flocks and herds; and the office of the chief shepherd was an important one.

entries.heading: Verse 10
entries.text: 1Sa 21:10-15 . At Gath He Feigns Himself Mad.

entries.heading: 13. feigned himself mad
entries.text: 13. feigned himself mad --It is supposed to have been an attack of epilepsy, real or perhaps only pretended. This disease is relieved by foaming at the mouth. let his spittle fall down upon his beard --No wonder that Achish supposed him insane, as such an indignity, whether done by another, or one's self, to the beard, is considered in the East an intolerable insult.
